title: Pancakes for Two
description: Light, fluffy pancakes made from scratch — perfect for a weekend breakfast. Simple ingredients, no electric mixer needed.

method.instruction: In a large bowl, whisk milk, egg, and vanilla extract together until well combined and slightly frothy, about 1 minute.
Sift self-raising flour and baking powder into the wet ingredients. Add caster sugar. Whisk gently until just combined — small lumps are fine, do not overmix.
Stir in melted butter until incorporated. The batter should be thick but pourable.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Lightly brush with butter.
Pour 60ml (1/4 cup) of batter per pancake into the pan (2-3 pancakes at a time, depending on pan size), leaving space between for spreading.
Cook for 2-3 minutes or until bubbles appear on the surface and the edges look set.
Flip and cook for another 1-2 minutes until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer to a plate and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with remaining batter, brushing the pan with butter between batches.
Serve pancakes topped with vanilla yoghurt, mixed berries, and a drizzle of golden syrup.

notes.title: Better by Hand
notes.content: For fluffier pancakes, whisk the wet ingredients (milk, egg, vanilla) first until frothy before adding dry ingredients. This incorporates air without overmixing the flour.

notes.title: Don't Overmix
notes.content: Overmixing develops gluten, resulting in tough, rubbery pancakes. Stir until flour is just incorporated — a few small lumps are fine.

notes.title: Test the Pan
notes.content: Flick a drop of water onto the pan — if it sizzles and evaporates immediately, the pan is ready.

notes.title: Keep Warm
notes.content: Place cooked pancakes on a baking sheet in a 100°C oven while you finish the batch.

notes.title: Add-ins
notes.content: Fold in 50g chocolate chips, fresh blueberries, or sliced banana after mixing the batter.
